message.content:
Los Angeles (Pacific Time) is normally **9 hours behind** Berlin (Central European Time).  
Because the U.S. and Europe change their clocks on slightly different dates, there are short periods each year when the difference is **8 hours**:

| Period | Los Angeles | Berlin | Difference |
|--------|-------------|--------|------------|
| Standard time (winter) | PST (UTC‑8) | CET (UTC+1) | 9 h |
| Early spring (US has switched to DST, Europe still on standard) | PDT (UTC‑7) | CET (UTC+1) | 8 h |
| Late summer/early fall (Europe has switched to DST, US still on standard) | PST (UTC‑8) | CEST (UTC+2) | 8 h |
| Summer (both on DST) | PDT (UTC‑7) | CEST (UTC+2) | 9 h |

So unless you’re looking at those brief transition weeks, you can safely assume a 9‑hour time difference.
